Antton Ugarte","authorUrl":null,"sourceProject":"Cooperapoly ","sourceProjectUrl":"https:\/\/www.behance.net\/gallery\/163677929\/Cooperapoly","behanceUrl":null,"id":"bcd68f29-16ed-451c-a9e8-1e893d83e8d7","imageUrl":"https:\/\/blog-assets.behance.net\/assets\/bcd68f29-16ed-451c-a9e8-1e893d83e8d7?format=webp&quality=90","alt":"Clara Briones Vedia and Antton Ugarte: Cooperapoly "},"content":"<p dir=\"ltr\">Rejection is an inevitable part of the creative journey. Whether it's a declined project proposal, a non-responsive client, or critical feedback on your work, rejection can feel deeply personal and discouraging. <\/p>\n<p dir=\"ltr\">Adopting the right mindset and strategies can help you turn these negative experiences into resilience building stepping stones to propel your career forward. Freelance creatives from Behance to share their experiences with rejection and their tips for bouncing back even stronger. <\/p>\n<h2 dir=\"ltr\">Don’t Take it Personally<\/h2>\n<p dir=\"ltr\">Rejection happens to all of us and although being told “no” stings, it’s important to remember that each rejection takes you one step closer to finding the right opportunity. “On many occasions I have come close to a dream project and lost it,” shares illustrator <a href=\"https:\/\/www.behance.net\/carolinasaiz\">Carolina Saiz<\/a>. “It happens to all of us.” <\/p>\n<div id=\"user-summary-target-1723067036654\" class=\"beComponents\" data-becomponent=\"miniprofile\" data-userid=\"5267013\"><\/div>\n<p>Carolina warns that a dangerous pitfall of rejection is turning the blame on yourself, but it’s important not to take rejection personally. “Most of the time it has nothing to do with your personality or your work, there are many other factors. And sometimes clients don't have the tact to understand that behind a budget there is a person.” Rather than taking rejection as a reflection of your worth, think of it as a stepping stone towards building your ideal creative career. <\/p>\n<p style=\"text-align: justify;\"><img loading=\"lazy\" src=\"https:\/\/blog-assets.behance.net\/assets\/f3ec5763-34cb-42d1-a0d6-02775df82eb6.jpg?width=3579&height=5031&format=webp&quality=90\" alt=\"Carolina\"><\/p>\n<h4 dir=\"ltr\"><a href=\"https:\/\/www.behance.net\/gallery\/182335685\/The-Sevillaner-cover\">The Sevillaner cover by Carolina Saiz<\/a><\/h4>\n<h2 dir=\"ltr\">Embrace the Learning Opportunity <\/h2>\n<p>Graphic designer <a href=\"https:\/\/www.behance.net\/clarabv\">Clara Briones Vedia<\/a> acknowledges that despite how commonplace rejection is, it can still take an emotional toll. “The first few times it affected me more, I felt frustration and sadness for a few days,” she recalls.<\/p>\n<div id=\"user-summary-target-1723065411526\" class=\"beComponents\" data-becomponent=\"miniprofile\" data-userid=\"3552365\"><\/div>\n<p>Understanding that rejection is a part of the creative process was crucial for Clara. “You realize that there are always new opportunities. Communication and empathy is key to being able to understand you and your customers. I no longer get frustrated if there is negative feedback, as long as the communication is clear and respectful.\"<\/p>\n<p><img loading=\"lazy\" src=\"https:\/\/blog-assets.behance.net\/assets\/a0fae242-eac6-47c1-8103-7c9f698aac22.jpg?width=3000&height=2000&format=webp&quality=90\" alt=\"Clara\"><\/p>\n<h4 dir=\"ltr\"><a href=\"https:\/\/www.behance.net\/gallery\/191531633\/Participaccion\">Participacción by Clara Briones Vedia and Antton Ugarte<\/a><\/h4>\n<p dir=\"ltr\">“I try to learn from my mistakes and be smarter next time,” adds Carolina. Her advice is to take rejection in stride, dust yourself off, and keep going: “Failure is useful if you learn from it.”<\/p>\n<h2 dir=\"ltr\">Set Realistic Expectations<\/h2>\n<p dir=\"ltr\">Setting realistic expectations can be a helpful tactic when dealing with rejection from new clients. \"I've had plenty of rejections in freelancing, especially with new clients,” says illustrator <a href=\"https:\/\/www.behance.net\/tvovchek\">Tatiana Vovchek<\/a>. <\/p>\n<div id=\"user-summary-target-1723065526780\" class=\"beComponents\" data-becomponent=\"miniprofile\" data-userid=\"838735\"><\/div>\n<p dir=\"ltr\">Over time, Tatiana has learned to manage her expectations and not dwell on projects that did not work out. “I'd say about 3-5% of the estimates I send out turn into real projects. So, I've gotten used to not hearing back at all after an estimate or receiving replies that don't lead anywhere,\" she says. Managing expectations helps you stay resilient and motivated, focusing on the opportunities that do materialize.<\/p>\n<p dir=\"ltr\"><img loading=\"lazy\" src=\"https:\/\/blog-assets.behance.net\/assets\/b5c76b74-fb9d-4055-8d43-e8fa32e42138.jpg?width=1500&height=1125&format=webp&quality=90\" alt=\"Tatiana\"><\/p>\n<h4 dir=\"ltr\"><a href=\"https:\/\/www.behance.net\/gallery\/154671525\/Best-friends-childrens-illustrations\">Best friends children's illustrations by Tatiana Vovchek<\/a><\/h4>\n<h2 dir=\"ltr\">Don’t Lose Your Confidence<\/h2>\n<p dir=\"ltr\">After a rejection, it’s a slippery slope to doubting your skills or the strength of your portfolio. For visual artist <a href=\"https:\/\/www.behance.net\/sebacestaro\">Sebastian Cestaro<\/a>, trusting yourself is the key to overcoming the self doubt that may creep in. \"I am always confident that there will be new opportunities and I am persistent with my work so those opportunities will come.” <\/p>\n<div id=\"user-summary-target-1723065423662\" class=\"beComponents\" data-becomponent=\"miniprofile\" data-userid=\"191360\"><\/div>\n<p dir=\"ltr\">Continuing to develop your portfolio will ultimately make you a better creative. “There are people who will be interested in my work and others who won't and it's totally understandable. I stay focused on my thing, working and sharing it because you never know who might be paying attention,” says Sebastian. <\/p>\n<p dir=\"ltr\"><img loading=\"lazy\" src=\"https:\/\/blog-assets.behance.net\/assets\/f41da904-2e9e-4167-973a-1c0086bf0fe6.jpg?width=3840&height=3840&format=webp&quality=90\" alt=\"Sebastian\"><\/p>\n<h4 dir=\"ltr\"><a href=\"https:\/\/www.behance.net\/gallery\/183678851\/The-Verge-Early-days-of-SEO\">The Verge - Early days of SEO by Sebastian Cestaro<\/a><\/h4>\n<p dir=\"ltr\">Tatiana also emphasizes trusting the journey and the process: “Your skills will improve gradually, and many of the clients you work with will improve too.” “Just follow your journey step by step,” she encourages. “The quantity will eventually turn into quality.”<\/p>\n<p dir=\"ltr\"><img loading=\"lazy\" src=\"https:\/\/blog-assets.behance.net\/assets\/acc9512f-d36c-4de4-adae-4b9e5656f11d.jpg?width=2800&height=1830&format=webp&quality=90\" alt=\"Riso\"><\/p>\n<h4 dir=\"ltr\"><a href=\"https:\/\/www.behance.net\/gallery\/159483389\/2023-risograph-CALENDAR\">2023 risograph CALENDAR by Clara Briones Vedia and Antton Ugarte<\/a><\/h4>\n<h2 dir=\"ltr\">Keep the Door Open<\/h2>\n<p dir=\"ltr\">Even when things don't work out, handle setbacks with honesty and empathy. Recently, illustrator <a href=\"https:\/\/www.behance.net\/denisfreitas\">Denis Freitas<\/a> declined a client project due to scheduling conflicts. “A large part of this situation boils down to knowing how to move forward and keeping the door open for future projects with that client,” says Denis.<\/p>\n<div id=\"user-summary-target-1723137166395\" class=\"beComponents\" data-becomponent=\"miniprofile\" data-userid=\"1545673\"><\/div>\n<p dir=\"ltr\">“Communication is key. I believe that presenting the truth in a human way always brings people closer.” Denis explained his scheduling issues and expressed his desire to work with the client in the future. “Thus, we move forward, doing the best we can with what we have.”<\/p>\n<p dir=\"ltr\"><img loading=\"lazy\" src=\"https:\/\/blog-assets.behance.net\/assets\/d23949ea-4942-4bb2-8dd3-72f14b96b6c8.jpg?width=1920&height=1323&format=webp&quality=90\" alt=\"Denis\"><\/p>\n<h4 dir=\"ltr\"><a href=\"https:\/\/www.behance.net\/gallery\/200930005\/Apple-Dragon-Boat-Festival\">Apple ● Dragon Boat Festival by Denis Freitas<\/a><\/h4>\n<h2 dir=\"ltr\">Exercise Your Power <\/h2>\n<p dir=\"ltr\">Remember that it’s a two-way street — as a creative, you are also in control when it comes to accepting and rejecting clients. \"Just as clients choose freelancers, you can choose your clients,\" reminds Tatiana. \"If a project doesn't feel like the right fit, it's okay to say no.\" <\/p>\n<p dir=\"ltr\">“There's always the right client for the right freelancer,” echoes Denis. By focusing on finding the right matches, freelancers can build more satisfying and productive working relationships. Adopting this mindset will empower you to seek out opportunities that align with your kills and values. <\/p>\n<p dir=\"ltr\" style=\"text-align: justify;\"><img loading=\"lazy\" src=\"https:\/\/blog-assets.behance.net\/assets\/9223a4e0-43dc-44a7-9ae4-4af8b9db3d85.jpg?width=1400&height=1857&format=webp&quality=90\" alt=\"Carolina2\"><\/p>\n<h4 dir=\"ltr\"><a href=\"https:\/\/www.behance.net\/gallery\/154584665\/National-Park-Map\">National Park Map by Carolina Saiz<\/a><\/h4>\n<h2 dir=\"ltr\">Find New Clients <\/h2>\n<p dir=\"ltr\">Get discovered by new clients by  your availability on Behance to let visitors to your profile know that you’re open to new freelance projects. You can also list a <a href=\"https:\/\/www.behance.net\/updates\/get-hired-on-behance-with-services\">Creative Service<\/a> for specific types of projects you’re available for. <\/p>\n<p dir=\"ltr\" style=\"text-align: justify;\"><a href=\"https:\/\/www.behance.net\/pro\" target=\"_blank\" rel=\"noopener\"><img loading=\"lazy\" src=\"https:\/\/blog-assets.behance.net\/assets\/fb5c0b4d-358a-4183-921e-86a3f0647f47.png?width=1765&height=172&format=webp&quality=90\" alt=\"Tiral Button With Padding\"><\/a><\/p>\n<p dir=\"ltr\">Upgrade to Behance Pro to unlock 0% platform fees on all freelance hiring transactions, as well as advanced analytics and project settings, Adobe Portfolio, and more.  <\/p>\n<p dir=\"ltr\"><a href=\"https:\/\/www.behance.net\/pro\" target=\"_blank\" rel=\"noopener\"><img loading=\"lazy\" src=\"https:\/\/blog-assets.behance.net\/assets\/cafacf28-5c7a-43e1-a650-92da1edb1ec4.png?width=2106&height=399&format=webp&quality=90\" alt=\"Blog Banner\"><\/a><\/p>"},{"id":1787,"slug":"personal-projects","title":"Beyond Client Work: The Power of Personal Projects","updatedOn":"2024-08-14T16:09:43.351Z","publishedOn":"2024-08-14T02:00:00.000Z","summary":"Freelance creatives from Behance discuss the power of personal projects and share their best practices for staying motivated while pursing both client and personal work. ","status":"published","keywords":[],"categories":[{"label":"Tips and Tutorials","slug":"tips-and-tutorials"}],"featuredImage":{"author":"Danny Ivan","authorUrl":"https:\/\/www.behance.net\/dannyivan","sourceProject":"Early Summer 2023 - Personal Studies","sourceProjectUrl":"https:\/\/www.behance.net\/gallery\/170753721\/Early-Summer-2023-Personal-Studies","behanceUrl":null,"id":"7f09863b-ec76-47a8-a3a5-a3b86c245778","imageUrl":"https:\/\/blog-assets.behance.net\/assets\/7f09863b-ec76-47a8-a3a5-a3b86c245778?format=webp&quality=90","alt":"Danny Ivan: Early Summer 2023 - Personal Studies"},"content":"<p dir=\"ltr\">Client work and personal projects are both integral components of a creative’s portfolio. While client projects demonstrate an artist’s ability to meet professional standards, personal projects provide a boundless opportunity for experimentation and self-expression. In addition to expanding your creative horizons, the skills learned from personal work can enhance the quality of future client work and the projects can even help attract new clients. <\/p>\n<p dir=\"ltr\">Freelance designers and artists from Behance discuss the significance of personal projects, and tips for incorporating them into your professional pursuits.<\/p>\n<h2 dir=\"ltr\">Approach Personal Work Without Pressure <\/h2>\n<p>Personal projects are intended to be a judgment-free space where you can express your creativity without any constraints, so there’s no need for pressure or stress. \"Personal projects are like your soul's home,” says 3D artist <a href=\"https:\/\/www.behance.net\/dannyivan\">Danny Ivan<\/a>. “They allow you to showcase what truly interests and excites you, providing inspiration and motivation for continuing your work.”<\/p>\n<div id=\"user-summary-target-1722278042745\" class=\"beComponents\" data-becomponent=\"miniprofile\" data-userid=\"252108\"><\/div>\n<p dir=\"ltr\">Danny pursues his personal projects during break or slow periods in his freelance work. His advice for staying consistent and motivated is to approach personal work with an ease of mind. “I keep it healthy without pressure or rush; it is more about a flow or idea, not a specific demand.”<\/p>\n<p dir=\"ltr\">Allowing himself to pursue creative interests without pressure has paid off for Danny. When he became fascinated with creating glass textures in 3D, he visited Murano Island in Italy to see how real glass sculptures were made. Abstract glassy textures have since then become a trend in technology imagery, and Danny had exactly the type of work that technology companies wanted to commission and license. “I felt lucky to be in the right time and place for tech brands to use my work.”<\/p>\n<p dir=\"ltr\" style=\"text-align: justify;\"><img loading=\"lazy\" src=\"https:\/\/blog-assets.behance.net\/assets\/139e6bca-2991-41de-8aa4-4429137328a7.jpg?width=1400&height=1980&format=webp&quality=90\" alt=\"Danny\"><\/p>\n<h4 dir=\"ltr\"><a href=\"https:\/\/www.behance.net\/gallery\/154269191\/Melted-3D-Glass\">Melted Glass by Danny Ivan<\/a><\/h4>\n<h2 dir=\"ltr\">Find Your Best Time <\/h2>\n<p dir=\"ltr\">Finding a schedule that works for you is crucial whether you’re working on personal projects or client work. “I understand that there are times when creativity is stronger, and other times when the capacity for execution is higher,” says designer and illustrator <a href=\"https:\/\/www.behance.net\/denisfreitas\">Denis Freitas<\/a>. These may be the same times for you, or may occur at different times in the day. <\/p>\n<div id=\"user-summary-target-1722278077884\" class=\"beComponents\" data-becomponent=\"miniprofile\" data-userid=\"1545673\"><\/div>\n<p dir=\"ltr\">For Denis, the morning is his most creative time, and the afternoon is when he is most productive, so he structures his day accordingly to make the most of his strengths. “I usually wake up a few hours earlier to dedicate myself to personal projects, typically for one to two hours. After that, I move on to commercial projects.” <\/p>\n<p dir=\"ltr\">Even if you’re not able to follow this schedule 100% of the time, having a guideline that optimizes your strengths throughout the day will have a positive impact on your productivity. “Although deadlines sometimes do not allow this routine to work perfectly, when I can follow it as planned, personal projects make my day better and my commercial work more complete,” reflects Denis.<\/p>\n<p dir=\"ltr\" style=\"text-align: justify;\"><img loading=\"lazy\" src=\"https:\/\/blog-assets.behance.net\/assets\/769114fb-db2f-4fcc-b3a2-c6b20f5637ae.jpg?width=1920&height=2053&format=webp&quality=90\" alt=\"Denis\"><\/p>\n<h4 dir=\"ltr\"><a href=\"https:\/\/www.behance.net\/gallery\/189936025\/Various-Illustrations-2023-2024\">Various Illustrations 2023 — 2024 by Denis Freitas<\/a><\/h4>\n<h2 dir=\"ltr\">Make it a Habit <\/h2>\n<p dir=\"ltr\">As with any habit, consistency is key. For Visual artist <a href=\"https:\/\/www.behance.net\/sebacestaro\">Sebastian Cestaro<\/a>, personal projects are a way for him to stay in constant learning. “Working on personal projects is important because it allows me to experiment and develop new ideas. Everything that arises when I explore new ways of expression, I apply to client work.”<\/p>\n<div id=\"user-summary-target-1722278135780\" class=\"beComponents\" data-becomponent=\"miniprofile\" data-userid=\"191360\"><\/div>\n<p dir=\"ltr\">Sebastian recognized the importance of consistency, and identified his most productive hours to make the most of his creativity. “My best times to work are in the morning and late afternoon to evening, those are the moments when I'm most focused. I made it a habit and it works for me.” <\/p>\n<p dir=\"ltr\">Like Denis, prioritization has helped Sebastian get the most out of his personal projects. “I organize myself by setting priorities, which involves focusing on what’s important and avoiding all kinds of distractions,” he shares. “Once I learned to focus and not waste time, the change was incredible.”<\/p>\n<p dir=\"ltr\" style=\"text-align: justify;\"><img loading=\"lazy\" src=\"https:\/\/blog-assets.behance.net\/assets\/f225bdc6-3570-436f-89cf-a58f36e9949c.jpg?width=2251&height=2813&format=webp&quality=90\" alt=\"Sebastian \"><\/p>\n<h4 dir=\"ltr\"><a href=\"https:\/\/www.behance.net\/gallery\/204288403\/This-is-Random-8-Personal-Project\">This is Random #8 - Personal Project by Sebastian Cestaro<\/a><\/h4>\n<h2 dir=\"ltr\">Give Yourself A Break <\/h2>\n<p dir=\"ltr\">Finding time for both personal and client work can be a challenge and overextending yourself means risking burnout. “A couple of years ago I was not able to find this balance and it unfortunately led to a burnout — a typical story,” recalls illustrator <a href=\"https:\/\/www.behance.net\/skom_olga\">Olga Skomorokhova<\/a>. Olga struggled to find motivation and balance in her work, finding herself rushing to meet deadlines for some projects and too engrossed in other projects. <\/p>\n<div id=\"user-summary-target-1722278165928\" class=\"beComponents\" data-becomponent=\"miniprofile\" data-userid=\"9951969\"><\/div>\n<p dir=\"ltr\">To avoid recurring burnout, Olga set boundaries. “Currently I am devoting at least one hour a day for personal projects during weekdays and as much as I want during weekends as I am not working on commissions on the days off.” <\/p>\n<p dir=\"ltr\">She also shows herself kindness and indulges in meaningful breaks to fully unplug when she needs it: “Sometimes I don’t have energy and motivation to work on something personal and then I allow myself to be lazy for some period. I believe that your body and mind will tell you when you’re ready.”<\/p>\n<p dir=\"ltr\"><img loading=\"lazy\" src=\"https:\/\/blog-assets.behance.net\/assets\/50ae1c3d-9786-4acf-93ec-aef53f2a07be.jpg?width=2500&height=2000&format=webp&quality=90\" alt=\"Olga\"><\/p>\n<h4 dir=\"ltr\"><a href=\"https:\/\/www.behance.net\/gallery\/110094819\/Illustrations-2020\">Illustrations 2020 by Olga Skomorokhova<\/a><\/h4>\n<h2 dir=\"ltr\">Showcase Your Work<\/h2>\n<p dir=\"ltr\">One of the unexpected joys of personal projects is that they can lead to client projects. Danny’s 3D exploration caught the eyes of technology companies. Olga created illustrations of pickles for her mother who enjoyed making pickles (the very first project she shared to Behance), and it’s since led to several commissions. <\/p>\n<p dir=\"ltr\"><img loading=\"lazy\" src=\"https:\/\/blog-assets.behance.net\/assets\/e111de21-56d3-4c89-8f4e-d356f22ff95c.png?width=1956&height=1018&format=webp&quality=90\" alt=\"Olga Pickles\"><\/p>\n<h4 dir=\"ltr\"><a href=\"https:\/\/www.behance.net\/gallery\/30472329\/Pickled-veggies\">Pickled veggies by Olga Skomorokhova<\/a><\/h4>\n<p dir=\"ltr\">Upload your personal work to Behance and get your talent seen by millions of creative professionals. Be sure to turn on the <a href=\"http:\/\/behance.net\/gethired\">Hire Me<\/a> feature in your profile to let visitors know that you’re open to new opportunities. ","updatedOn":"2024-09-11T14:43:39.998Z","publishedOn":"2024-07-31T11:00:00.000Z","summary":"Paul Lilley and Shalina Truelove, the husband and wife duo behind Ulysses Design Co., share why less it more when it comes to establishing a thriving design studio.","status":"published","keywords":[],"categories":[{"label":"Artist Spotlight","slug":"artist-spotlight"}],"featuredImage":{"author":"Ulysses Design Co","authorUrl":null,"sourceProject":"Palm Tree People Brand And Apparel Design","sourceProjectUrl":"https:\/\/www.behance.net\/gallery\/112575953\/Palm-Tree-People-Brand-And-Apparel-Design","behanceUrl":null,"id":"ae5be61e-ddad-4189-8ea6-813c862bfd87","imageUrl":"https:\/\/blog-assets.behance.net\/assets\/ae5be61e-ddad-4189-8ea6-813c862bfd87?format=webp&quality=90","alt":"Ulysses Design Co: Palm Tree People Brand And Apparel Design"},"content":"<p dir=\"ltr\"><a href=\"https:\/\/www.behance.net\/ulyssesdesignco\">Ulysses Design Co<\/a> is a boutique brand design studio run by husband and wife team Paul Lilley and Shalina Truelove. Based in Sydney, Australia, they specialize in hand drawn identity designs for independent food and beverage brands. <\/p>\n<p dir=\"ltr\">Before founding their studio, both Paul and Shalina came from creative backgrounds. Paul worked at global agencies including Vice and Cornerstone and Shalina at luxury fashion brands including Chanel and Dion Lee. <\/p>\n<div id=\"user-summary-target-1718299137590\" class=\"beComponents\" data-becomponent=\"miniprofile\" data-userid=\"592794853\"><\/div>\n<p dir=\"ltr\">“We started Ulysses Design Co in 2019 as we wanted to work more directly with boutique brands like our own, rather than being a cog in a big brand machine like our previous roles,” explains Paul. (The name of the studio is taken from Paul’s middle name. Fun fact: his full name, Paul Andrew Ulysses Lilley, spells out PAUL!) <\/p>\n<p><img loading=\"lazy\" src=\"https:\/\/blog-assets.behance.net\/assets\/6a8a18c5-3a5b-407e-acf8-e2ccae0f8c72.png?width=3335&height=2501&format=webp&quality=90\" alt=\"7c516e112575953.601762bd9041b\"><\/p>\n<h4 dir=\"ltr\"><a href=\"https:\/\/www.behance.net\/gallery\/112575953\/Palm-Tree-People-Brand-And-Apparel-Design\">Palm Tree People Brand And Apparel Design by Ulysses Design Co<\/a><\/h4>\n<p dir=\"ltr\">When they set out on their own, Paul and Shalina agreed to take a less is more approach by  focusing on their niche and building strong relationships with each of their clients. “We love to build relationships with our clients and become their creative partner for their brands, rather than a faceless freelancer.” <\/p>\n<p dir=\"ltr\">The Ulysses Design Co aesthetic is hand drawn, nostalgic branding, for progressive brands, and often takes inspiration from vintage hospitality branding and letterpress printing. “We love the subtle imperfections in this print medium and the warmth and authenticity of vintage branding,” shares Paul. From these influences, the studio creates contemporary identities that pay homage to tradition. <\/p>\n<p dir=\"ltr\"><img loading=\"lazy\" src=\"https:\/\/blog-assets.behance.net\/assets\/16bff6f8-8792-415a-a9cc-18bd84d8303b.png?width=1601&height=1200&format=webp&quality=90\" alt=\"303d5f156151279.636217b614830\"><\/p>\n<h4 dir=\"ltr\"><a href=\"https:\/\/www.behance.net\/gallery\/156151279\/Marketing-Campaign-for-Music-Festival\">Marketing Campaign for Music Festival by Ulysses Design Co<\/a><\/h4>\n<p dir=\"ltr\">“All our work is hand drawn, from our graphics to our custom logotype. We find this is a key component in our work and always produces original identities,” shares Paul. Over the years, this human touch has become something of a calling card for Ulysses Design Co, as clients appreciate the personalized and thoughtful approach they bring to each project. They’ve recently started creating their own fonts and selling them on Behance. <\/p>\n<div id=\"project-target-1720801901910\" class=\"beComponents\" data-becomponent=\"project\" data-projectid=\"188470443\"><\/div>\n<p dir=\"ltr\">“We found niching down really helped gain client trust and increased our value. Since we started to market ourselves as a food and drink specific branding studio we have had much more inquiries that have led to more projects and longer term relationships.”<\/p>\n<p dir=\"ltr\"><img loading=\"lazy\" src=\"https:\/\/blog-assets.behance.net\/assets\/d6f4da53-a8be-40ea-8091-9f28abc0d178.jpg?width=1820&height=1024&format=webp&quality=90\" alt=\"518bb5194547309.661f0b9156a13\"><\/p>\n<h4 dir=\"ltr\"><a href=\"https:\/\/www.behance.net\/gallery\/194547309\/Brand-Identity-For-Restaurant-Group\">Brand Identity For Restaurant Group by Ulysses Design Co<\/a><\/h4>\n<p dir=\"ltr\">Another key component of Ulysses Design Co’s success has been their investment in long-term relationships with their clients. They start every project with a strategy session to align themselves with the client, and through the process, present their work and gather feedback through short video calls or pre-recordings. “This allows us to explain our process and creative decisions with a human touch. Emails can be ambiguous and misinterpreted, we find cutting them out as much as possible helps produce better results and better relationships,” explains Paul. <\/p>\n<p dir=\"ltr\">The relationship doesn’t end when the project wraps. “We like to check in every few months to see how the business is going and offer free advice on brand management. This means we can give our clients super high value ongoing support and stay top of mind for new projects.” <\/p>\n<p dir=\"ltr\"><img loading=\"lazy\" src=\"https:\/\/blog-assets.behance.net\/assets\/7b102fc2-0d0b-4baf-8109-5f746a649cfa.png?width=1600&height=1200&format=webp&quality=90\" alt=\"Af15dd147606341.62c58c48baaca\"><\/p>\n<h4 dir=\"ltr\"><a href=\"https:\/\/www.behance.net\/gallery\/147606341\/Hand-Drawn-Rebrand-For-Filipino-Restaurant\">Hand Drawn Rebrand For Filipino Restaurant by Ulysses Design Co<\/a><\/h4>\n<p dir=\"ltr\">One of Ulysses Design Co’s long standing clients <a href=\"https:\/\/www.behance.net\/gallery\/194547309\/Brand-Identity-For-Restaurant-Group\">Pusit Pusit Hospitality<\/a> initially hired them to help with the rebrand of their fine dining restaurant <a href=\"https:\/\/www.behance.net\/gallery\/147606341\/Hand-Drawn-Rebrand-For-Filipino-Restaurant\">Musang<\/a>. Then again to brand their fast casual concept <a href=\"https:\/\/www.behance.net\/gallery\/184910273\/Brand-Identity-and-Graphics-for-Restaurant\">Kilig<\/a>, and then once more to brand their catering business <a href=\"https:\/\/www.behance.net\/gallery\/167398489\/Branding-For-Catering-Company\">Wild Cats<\/a>. Most recently, Paul and Shalina worked on the brand identity for the parent company.<\/p>\n<p dir=\"ltr\">“Your client is your friend, not your enemy. If you connect with them and gain alignment from the initial call the whole process will be high fives and back slaps rather than discontent and resentment,” says Paul.<\/p>\n<p dir=\"ltr\"><img loading=\"lazy\" src=\"https:\/\/blog-assets.behance.net\/assets\/3080dc36-e52f-47e7-b049-c93373ab11ae.png?width=3200&height=2400&format=webp&quality=90\" alt=\"C61ebd184910273.655ae911da3bf\"><\/p>\n<h4 dir=\"ltr\"><a href=\"https:\/\/www.behance.net\/gallery\/184910273\/Brand-Identity-and-Graphics-for-Restaurant\">Brand Identity and Graphics for Restaurant by Ulysses Design Co<\/a><\/h4>\n<p dir=\"ltr\">Behance has been a comprehensive platform for Paul and Shalina from the early days. “We use Behance for lots of different purposes, which is why it is our favorite platform!” says Paul. “We use it to showcase our work to potential clients, to build community and support fellow artists, to find inspiration, sell our digital products, and manage projects.”<\/p>\n<div id=\"project-target-1720805434980\" class=\"beComponents\" data-becomponent=\"project\" data-projectid=\"197437317\"><\/div>\n<p dir=\"ltr\">Paul and Shalina’s best tip for getting new clients is to “show the work you want to get.” and they’ve consistently shared their personal and client projects on Behance over the years. “All the case studies are on Behance and have led to lots of other projects with similar like minded food and drink brands. We love that the content is evergreen as we still get inquiries and new work from projects we posted years ago.” <\/p>\n<p dir=\"ltr\"><br><img loading=\"lazy\" src=\"https:\/\/blog-assets.behance.net\/assets\/7d247af2-af55-4ef8-9bdd-71f03f678885.jpg?width=3143&height=2335&format=webp&quality=90\" alt=\"6d50d7168896155.6442a1d6aa46c\"><\/p>\n<h4 dir=\"ltr\"><a href=\"https:\/\/www.behance.net\/gallery\/168896155\/West-Coast-Beer-Branding\">West Coast Beer Branding by Ulysses Design Co<\/a><\/h4>\n<p dir=\"ltr\">Since becoming <a href=\"http:\/\/behance.net\/pro\">Behance Pro<\/a> members, they’ve taken advantage of 0% platform fees to earn more on every project. “The main benefit to us was no platform fees on projects, which saves us hundreds of dollars on each project. Issuing contracts and taking payments through the platform helps make the admin process more efficient which allows us to spend more time on the creative side of things.”<\/p>\n<p><img loading=\"lazy\" src=\"https:\/\/blog-assets.behance.net\/assets\/823e21f6-bcc1-44f8-9404-c7e551efc8e5.gif?width=1820&height=1214&format=webp&quality=90\" alt=\"1e3f5e192739889.65e05e5462883\"><\/p>\n<h4 dir=\"ltr\"><a href=\"https:\/\/www.behance.net\/gallery\/192739889\/Yoga-With-Adriene-Apparel-Design\">Yoga With Adriene Apparel Design by Ulysses Design Co<\/a><\/h4>\n<p dir=\"ltr\">These days, Ulysses Design Co is booked several months out with clients. Maintaining a healthy work-life balance is essential for sustaining their creative energy and productivity. “We live on the coast so we try to go to the beach each morning before work. Being in nature really recharges our batteries and gets the creative juices flowing,” says Paul. <\/p>\n<p dir=\"ltr\">Running their own studio gives them greater flexibility with their schedule and work environment. “We have a home studio and get to see our toddler Nico plenty of times throughout the day too which is awesome as it reminds us why the heck we’re doing all this in the first place!”<\/p>\n<h4 dir=\"ltr\"><img loading=\"lazy\" src=\"https:\/\/blog-assets.behance.net\/assets\/437350a0-c42c-4c00-ac47-8b64189f9547.jpg?width=3333&height=2500&format=webp&quality=90\" alt=\"E1789f122839541.60e275272c174\"><\/h4>\n<h4 dir=\"ltr\"><a href=\"https:\/\/www.behance.net\/gallery\/122839541\/Tattoo-Parlour-Branding-for-TCO-London-99-Designs\">Tattoo Parlour Branding for TCO London & 99 Designs Ulysses Design Co<\/a><\/h4>\n<p dir=\"ltr\"><strong id=\"docs-internal-guid-93113825-7fff-bf63-fa1f-e860a15a591b\"><\/strong><a href=\"https:\/\/www.behance.net\/ulyssesdesignco\">See more work by Ulysses Design Co<\/a> and hire them for freelance projects on Behance.<\/p>"},{"id":1784,"slug":"2024-summer-olympics","title":"Featured Moodboard: 2024 Summer Olympics","updatedOn":null,"publishedOn":"2024-07-26T02:00:00.000Z","summary":"Celebrate the start of the 33rd Summer Olympic games in Paris with our curated moodboard. ","status":"published","keywords":[],"categories":[{"label":"Tips and Tutorials","slug":"tips-and-tutorials"}],"featuredImage":{"author":"Anastasia Statsenko","authorUrl":"Anastasia Statsenko","sourceProject":"FOUR! golfing range | LOGO DESIGN & BRAND IDENTITY ","sourceProjectUrl":"https:\/\/www.behance.net\/gallery\/163259927\/FOUR-golfing-range-LOGO-DESIGN-BRAND-IDENTITY","behanceUrl":null,"id":"885b772a-dfcc-47cc-af0a-0406f597bf29","imageUrl":"https:\/\/blog-assets.behance.net\/assets\/885b772a-dfcc-47cc-af0a-0406f597bf29?format=webp&quality=90","alt":"Anastasia Statsenko: FOUR! golfing range | LOGO DESIGN & BRAND IDENTITY "},"content":"<p dir=\"ltr\">Landing a new client is an exhilarating milestone, but it’s only the beginning. Building and nurturing relationships with clients is key to turning those first-time projects into long-term partnerships.<\/p>\n<p dir=\"ltr\">Repeat clients not only bring in steady work but also offer the chance to build lasting relationships and boost your reputation through referrals. We asked creatives who have found repeat customers on Behance to share their advice and practical tips for fostering client relationships and keep clients coming back. <\/p>\n<h2 dir=\"ltr\">1. Find Your Niche <\/h2>\n<p dir=\"ltr\">Clients are looking for creative professionals who have experience and expertise in specific fields, so honing your craft and carving out your niche is essential for standing out. Make sure your portfolio reflects the type of work you’re passionate about and the types of projects you want to be hired for. <\/p>\n<div id=\"user-summary-target-1718297177304\" class=\"beComponents\" data-becomponent=\"miniprofile\" data-userid=\"838735\"><\/div>\n<p dir=\"ltr\">Illustrator <a href=\"https:\/\/www.behance.net\/tvovchek\/projects\">Tatiana Vovchek<\/a> specializes in animal and children’s illustrations and she believes her commitment to her field keeps her clients coming back: “It is a niche of animal illustration and children illustration that I gradually chose for myself and stuck to for many years. It is my love for animals and nature which is felt through illustrations.” <\/p>\n<p dir=\"ltr\">Paul Lilley of <a href=\"https:\/\/www.behance.net\/ulyssesdesignco\">Ulysses Design Co<\/a> agrees. Paul founded his design studio with his wife and creative partner Shalina Truelove, and they have build a strong business specializing in nostalgic, hand-drawn branding designs. “We found niching down really helped gain client trust and increased our value,” shares Paul. Since we started to market ourselves as a food and drink specific branding studio we have had much more inquiries that have led to more projects and longer term relationships.”<\/p>\n<p dir=\"ltr\"><img loading=\"lazy\" src=\"https:\/\/blog-assets.behance.net\/assets\/86044377-0d73-4ed3-9ed6-dc56be50828d.jpg?width=2500&height=1843&format=webp&quality=90\" alt=\"85e98186180265.65e2448258847\"><\/p>\n<h4 dir=\"ltr\"><a href=\"https:\/\/www.behance.net\/gallery\/86180265\/Illustrations-for-IT-company\">Illustrations for IT company by Tatiana Vovchek<\/a><\/h4>\n<p>When clients see that you have a strong portfolio and a track record of successful projects within a specific niche, they are more likely to trust your abilities and feel confident that you can meet their unique needs.<\/p>\n<h2 dir=\"ltr\">2. Build Strong Relationships<\/h2>\n<p>Fostering strong, personal relationships with your clients can transform a transactional interaction into a long-term partnership. “We love to build relationships with our clients and become their creative partner for their brands, rather than a faceless freelancer,” says Paul Lilley of branding and identity design studio <a href=\"https:\/\/www.behance.net\/ulyssesdesignco\">Ulysses Design Co<\/a>. “We like to check in every few months to see how the business is going and offer free advice on brand management.”<\/p>\n<div id=\"user-summary-target-1718299137590\" class=\"beComponents\" data-becomponent=\"miniprofile\" data-userid=\"592794853\"><\/div>\n<p dir=\"ltr\">Clients will remember whether working with you was hard or easy, and this memory can significantly influence their decision to return for future projects. Effective communication and flexibility are crucial elements in retaining clients. Regular updates, transparent discussions about potential challenges, and proactive problem-solving can help prevent misunderstandings and keep the project running smoothly.2<\/p>\n<div id=\"user-summary-target-1720474783355\" class=\"beComponents\" data-becomponent=\"miniprofile\" data-userid=\"11475633\"><\/div>\n<p>“Balancing creative vision with client demands is a delicate process that requires effective communication, understanding the client's goals, and finding innovative solutions that meet both their needs and my artistic vision,” says creative director María Barón, who goes by <a href=\"https:\/\/www.behance.net\/susurrros\">Susurrros<\/a> on Behance. “Flexibility and adaptability are key in navigating this balance successfully,” she advises.<\/p>\n<p><img loading=\"lazy\" src=\"https:\/\/blog-assets.behance.net\/assets\/8b37912e-3c2b-4316-a17e-87d73f781889.jpg?width=3840&height=2560&format=webp&quality=90\" alt=\"A70b2c194746715.6601a7254bbb0\"><\/p>\n<h4 dir=\"ltr\"><a href=\"https:\/\/www.behance.net\/gallery\/194746715\/Nyxel-Paco\">Nyxel Paco by Susurrros (María Barón) and Javier Rojas<\/a><\/h4>\n<h2 dir=\"ltr\">3. Provide Extra Options and Flexibility<\/h2>\n<p dir=\"ltr\">By providing multiple options and being open to adjustments, you show that you value their preferences and are committed to finding the best solution for their project. Your willingness to experiment and collaborate with the client also builds a strong foundation for future projects. As clients experience your ability to deliver tailored, high-quality results, they are more likely to return to you for future work and recommend your services to others.<\/p>\n<div id=\"user-summary-target-1718298451382\" class=\"beComponents\" data-becomponent=\"miniprofile\" data-userid=\"1344550601\"><\/div>\n<p dir=\"ltr\">Illustrator <a href=\"https:\/\/www.behance.net\/tiagoleitao\">Tiago Leitao<\/a> has completed 36 freelance projects on Behance, many of them from repeat customers. His strategy is to offer unlimited sketches to help his clients arrive at a solution that meets their vision. <\/p>\n<p dir=\"ltr\">“In the early stages, I try to be clear about what I can provide and I like to offer unlimited initial sketches, to give the client the opportunity to choose their preferred direction and ensure that the final result matches their vision,” says Tiago. “I'm always open to experimenting new design forms and themes, as long as it aligns with my style.”<\/p>\n<p style=\"text-align: justify;\"><img loading=\"lazy\" src=\"https:\/\/blog-assets.behance.net\/assets\/d4e83760-10c0-4c44-bb35-b3e5d59d683b.png?width=1034&height=1030&format=webp&quality=90\" alt=\"Screen Shot 2024 06 13 at 1.08.33 Pm\"><\/p>\n<h4 dir=\"ltr\"><a href=\"https:\/\/www.behance.net\/gallery\/198043769\/Client-Illustrations\">Client illustrations by Tiago Leitao<\/a><\/h4>\n<h2 dir=\"ltr\">4. Provide Extra Value <\/h2>\n<p dir=\"ltr\">Under promise and over deliver to exceed your client’s expectations. Providing additional value through recommendations, supporting materials or extra services shows your commitment to your client’s success and builds a long-lasting relationship. <\/p>\n<p dir=\"ltr\">“Client success is my success,” says Tatiana. “If I have a chance to overdeliver — for example, give my recommendations to marketing visuals of the product, prepare print files, make a reel with illustration process for the book promotion, or make professional photos of the product as I have a photography background — I will be glad to help!”<\/p>\n<p dir=\"ltr\"><img loading=\"lazy\" src=\"https:\/\/blog-assets.behance.net\/assets\/866f4170-73b8-42a8-a47e-3dc2c66b4101.jpg?width=1600&height=1200&format=webp&quality=90\" alt=\"6e85bb157783375.637f3d07e6b69\"><\/p>\n<h4 dir=\"ltr\"><a href=\"https:\/\/www.behance.net\/gallery\/157783375\/Branding-For-Casual-Restaurant\">Branding For Casual Restaurant by Ulysses Design Co.<\/a><\/h4>\n<h2 dir=\"ltr\">5. Maintain Contact Post-Project<\/h2>\n<p dir=\"ltr\">Stay in touch with clients even after a project has wrapped. Offering post-project support and assistance can help reinforce your reliability and dedication, encouraging clients to return for future work. <\/p>\n<p dir=\"ltr\">“I strive to always deliver more than what's expected,” says brand designer <a href=\"https:\/\/www.behance.net\/jmvr\">Jose Manuel Vega<\/a>. “After completing the project, I maintain contact with clients to see if I can assist with its release or ongoing management.”<\/p>\n<div id=\"user-summary-target-1718298956852\" class=\"beComponents\" data-becomponent=\"miniprofile\" data-userid=\"9760199\"><\/div>\n<p dir=\"ltr\">Graphic designer <a href=\"https:\/\/www.behance.net\/stacysdesign\">Anastasia Statsenko<\/a> also emphasizes the importance of getting feedback: “Seek feedback regularly to improve and refine your approach, fostering loyalty and long-term partnerships.”<\/p>\n<div id=\"user-summary-target-1720474808866\" class=\"beComponents\" data-becomponent=\"miniprofile\" data-userid=\"1377177195\"><\/div>\n<p dir=\"ltr\">Client feedback helps you become a better designer and strengthens client management skills by providing valuable insights into their preferences and expectations, allowing you to tailor your approach and communication more effectively in future projects.<\/p>\n<p><img loading=\"lazy\" src=\"https:\/\/blog-assets.behance.net\/assets\/36e7fda6-c162-4aaa-8462-0441219846bb.jpg?width=3840&height=2469&format=webp&quality=90\" alt=\"9afbe3176420649.64c43add84228\"><\/p>\n<h4 dir=\"ltr\"><a href=\"https:\/\/www.behance.net\/gallery\/176420649\/OUNCE-BAR-LOGO-DESIGN-BRAND-IDENTITY\">OUNCE BAR | LOGO DESIGN & BRAND IDENTITY by Anastasia Statsenko<\/a><\/h4>\n<h2 dir=\"ltr\">6. Deliver High Quality Work <\/h2>\n<p dir=\"ltr\">At the end of the day, clients are looking for results. They want high-quality work that matches their brief, meets their expectations, and helps them achieve their goals. When clients are satisfied, it not only reflects positively on your work but also strengthens the relationship for future collaborations.<\/p>\n<p dir=\"ltr\">“It’s crucial to deliver high-quality work within the agreed timelines and ensure that the client is happy with the end result,” says Tiago. “Working with a client is teamwork, and when the end result is incredible it's not just because of me.” <\/p>\n<h4 dir=\"ltr\"><img loading=\"lazy\" src=\"https:\/\/blog-assets.behance.net\/assets\/c31542c9-4e2d-4325-8f59-23c4406d9693.jpg?width=2833&height=1889&format=webp&quality=90\" alt=\"E08c89168857079.6441ccd0561de\"><\/h4>\n<h4 dir=\"ltr\"><a href=\"https:\/\/www.behance.net\/gallery\/168857079\/Venali\">Venali by Jose Manuel Vega<\/a><\/h4>\n<h2 dir=\"ltr\">Find New Clients on Behance<\/h2>\n<p dir=\"ltr\"><a href=\"http:\/\/behance.net\/gethired\">Update your availability<\/a> on Behance to let visitors to your profile know that you’re open to new freelance projects or full-time positions. You can also list a <a href=\"https:\/\/www.behance.net\/updates\/get-hired-on-behance-with-services\">Creative Service<\/a> for specific types of projects you’re available for. <\/p>\n<p style=\"text-align: justify;\"><a href=\"https:\/\/www.behance.net\/pro\" target=\"_blank\" rel=\"noopener\"><img loading=\"lazy\" src=\"https:\/\/blog-assets.behance.net\/assets\/5522b20d-ca83-4685-8678-a1b25ae42a8e.png?width=1765&height=172&format=webp&quality=90\" alt=\"Tiral Button With Padding\"><\/a><\/p>\n<p dir=\"ltr\">Upgrade to <a href=\"http:\/\/behance.net\/pro\">Behance Pro<\/a> to unlock 0% platform fees on all freelance hiring transactions, as well as advanced analytics and project settings, Adobe Portfolio, and more.  <\/p>\n<p dir=\"ltr\"><a href=\"https:\/\/www.behance.net\/pro\" target=\"_blank\" rel=\"noopener\"><img loading=\"lazy\" src=\"https:\/\/blog-assets.behance.net\/assets\/ce3efee7-5179-420d-955c-fb9171dc0d14.png?width=2106&height=399&format=webp&quality=90\" alt=\"Blog Banner\"><\/a><\/p>"},{"id":1751,"slug":"how-to-stay-motivated","title":"How to Stay Motivated When Work Slows Down","updatedOn":"2024-07-09T17:09:45.108Z","publishedOn":"2024-07-09T17:00:00.000Z","summary":"Effective strategies for maintaining momentum and staying productive during slow work periods.","status":"published","keywords":[],"categories":[{"label":"Tips and Tutorials","slug":"tips-and-tutorials"}],"featuredImage":{"author":"Tatiana Vovchek","authorUrl":"https:\/\/www.behance.net\/tvovchek","sourceProject":"Unreal People ","sourceProjectUrl":"https:\/\/www.behance.net\/gallery\/151088655\/Unreal-people","behanceUrl":null,"id":"202b2559-cd62-4b5e-aa31-5e48ba04ac69","imageUrl":"https:\/\/blog-assets.behance.net\/assets\/202b2559-cd62-4b5e-aa31-5e48ba04ac69?format=webp&quality=90","alt":"Tatiana Vovchek: Unreal People "},"content":"<p dir=\"ltr\">For freelance creatives, encountering slow periods is inevitable. While these lulls can be challenging both emotionally and financially, they also present an opportunity and challenge to grow, improve, and prepare for the future. <\/p>\n<p dir=\"ltr\">We asked experienced designers from Behance about overcoming the slump and their advice for staying motivated and productive when work slows down. <\/p>\n<h2 dir=\"ltr\">1. Focus on Personal Development<\/h2>\n<p dir=\"ltr\">Slower times give you the bandwidth to pursue personal growth, which is an essential part of furthering your skill set and ultimately, your career. “During slower periods, I stay motivated by focusing on personal development, exploring new design trends, and networking within the industry,” says <a href=\"https:\/\/www.behance.net\/susurrros\">María Barón<\/a>, a freelance creative director who goes by Susurrros on Behance, Setting short-term goals, such as updating her portfolio or acquiring new skills, also helps María maintain productivity and momentum. <\/p>\n<div id=\"user-summary-target-1714693522147\" class=\"beComponents\" data-becomponent=\"miniprofile\" data-userid=\"11475633\"><\/div>\n<p dir=\"ltr\">Some effective ways to focus on personal growth include enrolling in online courses to learn new skills or improve existing ones, and staying updated with the latest design trends through Behance, social media, and industry publications to find fresh inspiration. <\/p>\n<p dir=\"ltr\"><img loading=\"lazy\" src=\"https:\/\/blog-assets.behance.net\/assets\/bb8de99c-67a8-47c0-89fc-9763a1390141?width=1920&height=1080&format=webp&quality=90\" alt=\"473f1b188189861.65982aaec5134\"><\/p>\n<h4 dir=\"ltr\"><a href=\"https:\/\/www.behance.net\/gallery\/188189861\/Medicina-Alternativa?tracking_source=project_owner_other_projects\">Medicina Alternativa by Susurrros (María Barón)<\/a><\/h4>\n<h2 dir=\"ltr\">2. Expand Your Potential Client List <\/h2>\n<p dir=\"ltr\">With Behance, you can showcase your work to millions of creative professionals and potential clients. <a href=\"http:\/\/behance.net\/gethired\">Update your availability<\/a> to let visitors to your profile know that you’re available for new work, and to be included in our directory of freelancers. You can also list a <a href=\"https:\/\/www.behance.net\/updates\/get-hired-on-behance-with-services?tracking_source=footer_static_\">Creative Service<\/a> to advertise specific projects you’re available for.  <\/p>\n<h2 dir=\"ltr\">3. Show the Work You Want to Get<\/h2>\n<p dir=\"ltr\">Showcasing the type of projects you want to get hired for helps you build a strong portfolio that aligns with your goals, and helps attract clients who value your style and approach. Paul Lilley of Sydney based studio <a href=\"https:\/\/www.behance.net\/ulyssesdesignco\">Ulysses Design Co<\/a> recalls the initial struggle to find clients in the early days of his business: “We’re lucky enough to be booked out for 1-2 months in advance these days, but when we were starting out getting clients was a struggle.”<\/p>\n<div id=\"user-summary-target-1716484395265\" class=\"beComponents\" data-becomponent=\"miniprofile\" data-userid=\"592794853\"><\/div>\n<p dir=\"ltr\">Paul’s advice for finding new clients is to show the work you want to get. “Whenever we want to develop our aesthetic or target, we create a bunch of work in this style and share it on Behance,” he shares. Projects like <a href=\"https:\/\/www.behance.net\/gallery\/168896155\/West-Coast-Beer-Branding\">West Coast Beer Branding<\/a>, <a href=\"https:\/\/www.behance.net\/gallery\/182057521\/Bottle-Shop-Branding\">Bottle Shop Branding<\/a>, and <a href=\"https:\/\/www.behance.net\/gallery\/169863353\/Palm-Beach-Cafe-Branding\">Palm Beach Cafe <\/a>were all created as a part of Ulysses’s strategy to develop their portfolio and attract clients from specific industries looking to hire them for their laid back retro style. <\/p>\n<p dir=\"ltr\" style=\"text-align: justify;\"><img loading=\"lazy\" src=\"https:\/\/blog-assets.behance.net\/assets\/b3962308-9bd3-4dc0-8ecb-9ff64494cb7c?width=3200&height=2400&format=webp&quality=90\" alt=\"Palm Beach Cafe\"><\/p>\n<h4 dir=\"ltr\"><a href=\"https:\/\/www.behance.net\/gallery\/169863353\/Palm-Beach-Cafe-Branding\">Palm Beach Cafe Branding by Ulysses Design Co<\/a><\/h4>\n<h2 dir=\"ltr\">4. Embrace Passion Projects<\/h2>\n<p dir=\"ltr\">Personal projects give you the freedom to exercise your creative expression without restraints. They are a great opportunity to experiment with new styles or tools, expand your skill set, and as Paul mentioned, create the work you want to be hired for. “Doing passion projects is vital for both sanity and morale!” says freelance designer <a href=\"https:\/\/www.behance.net\/alancheetham_studio\">Alan Cheetham<\/a>. <\/p>\n<div id=\"user-summary-target-1715268530130\" class=\"beComponents\" data-becomponent=\"miniprofile\" data-userid=\"583371\"><\/div>\n<p dir=\"ltr\">When Alan enters slower periods with his schedule, he turns to his notebook. “I open up my notes on my phone and realize how many unrealized ideas I've made in the last decades and think, here's the time to attempt to tick off some of these. Sometimes it's just refreshingly simple to create art\/design without a brief.<\/p>\n<p dir=\"ltr\"><img loading=\"lazy\" src=\"https:\/\/blog-assets.behance.net\/assets\/7eb21442-2e61-48fc-8b54-6fdbbe191466?width=2324&height=1700&format=webp&quality=90\" alt=\"Screen Shot 2024 05 23 at 1.20.57 Pm\"><\/p>\n<h4 dir=\"ltr\"><a href=\"https:\/\/www.behance.net\/gallery\/153808295\/Various-illustration-collaborations-2021-2022\">Various illustration collaborations 2021-2022 by Alan Cheetham<\/a><\/h4>\n<h2 dir=\"ltr\">5. Keep a Project Backlog <\/h2>\n<p dir=\"ltr\">Having a backlog of projects ensures you’re never without something to work on. These could be those personal projects, but they could also be administrative or organizational tasks that can help you streamline your workflow or build your business. <\/p>\n<div id=\"user-summary-target-1714693180683\" class=\"beComponents\" data-becomponent=\"miniprofile\" data-userid=\"199493\"><\/div>\n<p dir=\"ltr\">Digital designer Lorenzo Bocchi keeps a running list of things that he can work on during slower times — things that are often overlooked or deprioritized when his schedule is busier. “I have about 50 projects to work on case studies for. I have a backlog of things to do to maintain and improve my internal tools like my own design system, my Webflow builder started, brand strategy processes, and a social media planner.” <\/p>\n<p style=\"text-align: justify;\"><img loading=\"lazy\" src=\"https:\/\/blog-assets.behance.net\/assets\/ced6805e-852c-44fd-bf17-9e0c6e3343ee?width=1908&height=1462&format=webp&quality=90\" alt=\"Screen Shot 2024 06 19 at 2.17.44 Pm\"><\/p>\n<h4 dir=\"ltr\"><a href=\"https:\/\/www.behance.net\/gallery\/142200827\/Hello-Coach\" target=\"_blank\" rel=\"noopener\">Hello Coach by Lorenzo Bocchi<\/a><\/h4>\n<h2 dir=\"ltr\">6. Expand Your Income Streams<\/h2>\n<p dir=\"ltr\"><br><a href=\"https:\/\/www.behance.net\/blog\/sell-downloadable-assets-on-behance\">Digital assets<\/a> offer creatives the opportunity to earn passive income alongside their freelance projects. Illustrator <a href=\"https:\/\/www.behance.net\/tvovchek\/\">Tatiana Vovchek<\/a> supplements her income as a freelance illustrator by offering vectors and pattern designs as assets on Behance. “ It is my way to build a passive income stream and to give a second life to illustrations I made for personal study or which were not used by clients,” she shares.<\/p>\n<div id=\"user-summary-target-1716485361822\" class=\"beComponents\" data-becomponent=\"miniprofile\" data-userid=\"838735\"><\/div>\n<p dir=\"ltr\">In addition to bringing her additional revenue, her assets have helped her find new clients: “I got a client who offered me a pattern design project through Behance having looked at the assets I put on sale.”<\/p>\n<p dir=\"ltr\"><img loading=\"lazy\" src=\"https:\/\/blog-assets.behance.net\/assets\/31d923fa-b782-4740-9859-2a53721eeb22?width=1500&height=1125&format=webp&quality=90\" alt=\"D5a665131736211.6358fc190aa2d\"><\/p>\n<h4 dir=\"ltr\"><a href=\"https:\/\/www.behance.net\/gallery\/131736211\/100-DOGS-ILLUSTRATIONS-FOR-PET-BLOG\">100+ DOGS ILLUSTRATIONS FOR PET BLOG by Tatiana Vovchek <\/a><\/h4>\n<p dir=\"ltr\"><a href=\"https:\/\/www.behance.net\/blog\/sell-downloadable-assets-on-behance\">Attach downloadable files<\/a> to a new or existing Behance project to start monetizing your content to a global community of over 50 million members. You can specify the type of license, set your own price for each asset, and continue to monetize on other platforms. There is no fee to list your assets, but with each sale, you’ll be subject to a 30% platform fee. <a href=\"http:\/\/behance.net\/pro\">Upgrade to Behance Pro<\/a> to eliminate platform fees on all sales you make. <\/p>\n<p dir=\"ltr\" style=\"text-align: justify;\"><a href=\"https:\/\/www.behance.net\/pro\" target=\"_blank\" rel=\"noopener\"><img loading=\"lazy\" src=\"https:\/\/blog-assets.behance.net\/assets\/a4fc8494-fa0b-42f0-b35c-1baf16bf8a85?width=1765&height=172&format=webp&quality=90\" alt=\"Tiral Button With Padding\"><\/a><\/p>\n<p dir=\"ltr\">While the slowdown of work can be disheartening, it can be an opportunity for you to recharge, refine your skills, and explore new horizons. Remember this phase is temporary, and with the right  mindself, you can turn it into a bountiful opportunity for growth. <\/p>\n<p dir=\"ltr\"><a href=\"https:\/\/www.behance.net\/pro\" target=\"_blank\" rel=\"noopener\"><img loading=\"lazy\" src=\"https:\/\/blog-assets.behance.net\/assets\/5334e5c8-7375-4d26-8d85-5e09b63977c0?width=2106&height=399&format=webp&quality=90\" alt=\"Blog Banner\"><\/a><\/p>"},{"id":1750,"slug":"halit-benli","title":"Behance Artist Spotlight: Halit Benli","updatedOn":"2024-06-25T18:03:35.740Z","publishedOn":"2024-06-27T01:10:00.000Z","summary":"Designer and digital artist Halit Benli on building his portfolio and finding new clients through Behance. ","status":"published","keywords":[],"categories":[{"label":"Artist Spotlight","slug":"artist-spotlight"}],"featuredImage":{"author":"Halit Benli","authorUrl":"https:\/\/www.behance.net\/halitbenli","sourceProject":"Masked Realms: Psychedelic Faces ","sourceProjectUrl":null,"behanceUrl":"https:\/\/www.behance.net\/gallery\/190836723\/Masked-Realms-Psychedelic-Faces","id":"bd92ff73-90b2-40f2-9790-3d6692e4ad46","imageUrl":"https:\/\/blog-assets.behance.net\/assets\/bd92ff73-90b2-40f2-9790-3d6692e4ad46?format=webp&quality=90","alt":"Halit Benli: Masked Realms: Psychedelic Faces "},"content":"<p>“My art journey started when I was 13,” recalls designer and digital artist <a href=\"https:\/\/www.behance.net\/halitbenli\" target=\"_blank\" rel=\"noopener\">Halit Benli<\/a>. “At that time, I was simply drawing and painting my surroundings with basic drawing knowledge. Then I took a step towards studying painting in a fine arts high school with the support of my teacher.”<\/p>\n<div id=\"user-summary-target-1718378118463\" class=\"beComponents\" data-becomponent=\"miniprofile\" data-userid=\"74777871\"><\/div>\n<p dir=\"ltr\">It wasn’t until Halit went on to university that he discovered graphic design as a discipline, a moment he describes as life-changing. “It was a completely different area than what I was familiar with, and there were many struggles at the beginning,” Halit shares.<\/p>\n<p dir=\"ltr\">Although he enjoyed the design process, Halit felt like something was missing. “I always wanted to find a way to create and express my feelings,” he explains. <\/p>\n<p dir=\"ltr\" style=\"text-align: justify;\"><img loading=\"lazy\" src=\"https:\/\/blog-assets.behance.net\/assets\/302266c9-e72b-4ce3-bf57-410204198160?width=3000&height=3750&format=webp&quality=90\" alt=\"B07950190330897.65b946ca5e781\"><\/p>\n<h4 dir=\"ltr\"><a href=\"https:\/\/www.behance.net\/gallery\/190330897\/Autoportrait\">Autoportrait by Halit Benli<\/a><\/h4>\n<p dir=\"ltr\">Halit began experimenting with different art forms to find his creative voice. His eureka moment came when he traveled to Poland with the Erasmus Program. “I gained a totally different perspective on life, art, and design. I learned to think and see more visually and to create powerful artworks, which led me to create more experimental works. I was able to rediscover myself.”<\/p>\n<p dir=\"ltr\" style=\"text-align: justify;\"><img loading=\"lazy\" src=\"https:\/\/blog-assets.behance.net\/assets\/c5c2992c-5e73-499b-a10d-3961b964fcf7?width=3000&height=3750&format=webp&quality=90\" alt=\"22029b183745915.65451169ab606\"><\/p>\n<h4 dir=\"ltr\"><a href=\"https:\/\/www.behance.net\/gallery\/183745915\/Psychedelic-Horizons-Sunlit-Realms\">Psychedelic Horizons: Sunlit Realms by Halit Benli<\/a><\/h4>\n<p dir=\"ltr\">Halit challenged himself to create art every day for over a year to help him develop his personal style. “I experimented with new software, techniques, tools, and everything I could,” he recalls. “I even got my first freelance job on Behance at the beginning of it, which encouraged me to continue!” <\/p>\n<p dir=\"ltr\">Today, Halit calls himself an experimental digital artist. “The works I create are generally composed of reflections from the world I create inside my mind,” he explains. “Every day, by producing a piece, I try to expand the reality of this abstract world a little more. The works are meticulously crafted with layers, and the deeper you delve, the more intricacies you can discover, much like the world we live in.”<\/p>\n<p dir=\"ltr\" style=\"text-align: justify;\"><img loading=\"lazy\" src=\"https:\/\/blog-assets.behance.net\/assets\/c9b55e2d-5428-4bd6-8dad-2f7ae115f8c9?width=2800&height=3500&format=webp&quality=90\" alt=\"9ed117164349289.63f567d628ce7\"><\/p>\n<h4 dir=\"ltr\"><a href=\"https:\/\/www.behance.net\/gallery\/164349289\/First-Round-of-My-Everyday-Challenge\">First Round of My Everyday Challenge by Halit Benli<\/a><\/h4>\n<p dir=\"ltr\">Halit has been a Behance member since 2017. “Initially, it was just an art platform where I uploaded my works to have them on the internet, but it has since become my main portfolio. I am now trying to update my works more frequently, and this process allows me to showcase my style to people and potential clients on Behance.” <\/p>\n<div id=\"service-card-target-1718380379070\" class=\"beComponents\" data-becomponent=\"service\" data-username=\"halitbenli\" data-serviceid=\"118929\"><\/div>\n<p dir=\"ltr\">In addition to using Behance as his portfolio, Halit has been able to expand his network and find new clients through the platform. “Most of the time, clients reach out to me through my services or direct inquiries on Behance.”<\/p>\n<p dir=\"ltr\">Halit is no stranger to freelancing, but he recently decided to pursue it full-time. A crucial step Halit took as a part of that transition was making sure that he had financial stability. “Having enough money saved up for five or six months can alleviate financial worries and anxieties about finding freelance work. This has been one of the biggest challenges for me before starting full-time freelancing, and having financial stability can make the transition smoother.”<\/p>\n<p dir=\"ltr\" style=\"text-align: justify;\"><img loading=\"lazy\" src=\"https:\/\/blog-assets.behance.net\/assets\/a0ac6000-aece-4ca7-9d66-e3e745dd96e0?width=3000&height=3750&format=webp&quality=90\" alt=\"42855a190327175.65b93c8f742c8\"><\/p>\n<h4 dir=\"ltr\"><a href=\"https:\/\/www.behance.net\/gallery\/190327175\/Mindscapes-A-Psychedelic-Exploration\">Mindscapes: A Psychedelic Exploration by Halit Benli<\/a><\/h4>\n<p dir=\"ltr\">Over the years, he’s picked up many valuable lessons about working with clients as well. “I always listen to the clients, understand what they ask for and need, and then combine these requirements with my art vision,” he shares. <\/p>\n<p dir=\"ltr\">One mistake he learned the hard way was jumping into client projects without fully understanding the client or the scope of the work. “Sometimes, even if a project sounds cool, it might not be a good match,” says Halit. <\/p>\n<p style=\"text-align: justify;\"><img loading=\"lazy\" src=\"https:\/\/blog-assets.behance.net\/assets\/1a3f5891-f524-4209-b313-e2acefe3e643?width=3000&height=3750&format=webp&quality=90\" alt=\"Ffc476196078389.661956a0f15b0\"><\/p>\n<h4 dir=\"ltr\"><a href=\"https:\/\/www.behance.net\/gallery\/196078389\/Divine-Watch\">Divine Watch by Halit Benli<\/a><\/h4>\n<p dir=\"ltr\">Halit’s unique vision and his commitment to his craft has helped him build a network of returning clients. He often creates work beyond the ask to fully explore the possibilities and find the right solution. <\/p>\n<p dir=\"ltr\">“When I start a project and if I'm having fun, I like to see a few more options for myself. So I don't mind if I create one or five; it doesn't matter as long as I'm enjoying it. While doing this, I've realized customers notice that I'm deeply invested in the project.\"<\/p>\n<p dir=\"ltr\" style=\"text-align: justify;\"><img loading=\"lazy\" src=\"https:\/\/blog-assets.behance.net\/assets\/5cd6c66d-0b7f-49dc-b4d1-00164a12dc8a?width=1000&height=1000&format=webp&quality=90\" alt=\"56f9d9141554325.62a663cc96dcf\"><\/p>\n<h4 dir=\"ltr\"><a href=\"https:\/\/www.behance.net\/gallery\/141554325\/NODELTA-Psy-Pattern-Series\">NO\/DELTA Psy-Pattern Series by Halit Benli<\/a><\/h4>\n<p dir=\"ltr\">When Halit was commissioned to create an album cover and two to three accompanying looping animations for NO\/DELTA, he ended up creating over 15 variations. “I was having fun and couldn't stop myself,” he reflects. <\/p>\n<p dir=\"ltr\">He shared the additional variations with the client and gave them the option to pay for the additional work, or to keep the assets for free. \"They ended up paying extra for my work. I realized people like this kind of approach,” says Halit. <\/p>\n<p dir=\"ltr\" style=\"text-align: justify;\"><img loading=\"lazy\" src=\"https:\/\/blog-assets.behance.net\/assets\/decfeefa-6a2d-4b63-b220-617a15362b6d?width=3000&height=3750&format=webp&quality=90\" alt=\"07ba6d183492059.656107a59d2cb\"><\/p>\n<h4 dir=\"ltr\"><a href=\"https:\/\/www.behance.net\/gallery\/183492059\/A-Visual-Odyssey-of-Emotions\">A Visual Odyssey of Emotions by Halit Benli<\/a><\/h4>\n<p dir=\"ltr\">See more work by Halit and hire him for freelance projects on <a href=\"https:\/\/www.behance.net\/halitbenli\">Behance<\/a>. <\/p>"}],"featuredCreatives":[{"name":"Cranio Dsgn ","url":"https:\/\/www.behance.net\/craniodsgn","summary":"Alex Garcia A.K.A Cranio Dsgn creates retro-pop vector art with a contemporary touch, combining vibrant colors and expressive emotions.","avatarId":"7ebc3265-8a90-4792-a5d0-8a62fe876e25","creativeCategories":[{"name":"Illustration","url":"https:\/\/www.behance.net\/search\/users?field=illustration"}],"avatarImage":"https:\/\/blog-assets.behance.net\/assets\/7ebc3265-8a90-4792-a5d0-8a62fe876e25?format=webp&quality=90"},{"name":"Anastasia Statsenko","url":"https:\/\/www.behance.net\/stacysdesign","summary":"Anastasia is a California-based graphic designer who specializes in creating colorful and bold branding and identity designs.","avatarId":"f98b9799-5601-4148-9ed1-f4a5408e63df","creativeCategories":[{"name":"Graphic Design","url":"https:\/\/www.behance.net\/search\/users?field=graphic+design"}],"avatarImage":"https:\/\/blog-assets.behance.net\/assets\/f98b9799-5601-4148-9ed1-f4a5408e63df?format=webp&quality=90"},{"name":"Lana Burlachuk","url":"https:\/\/www.behance.net\/lanaburlachuk","summary":"Lana is a self-taught designer who got her start in packaging and branding design when she started her own oatmeal company.       <header class="article-header">
        <div title="Behance and Adobe Firefly FAQ" class="article-title">
          Behance and Adobe Firefly FAQ
          
        
              <div class="meta-data">Updated  <time datetime="2023-03-21T13:13:52Z" title="03/21/2023, 08:13" data-datetime="relative">2 years ago</time>  </div>
      </div></header>
      <section class="article-info">
        <div class="article-content">
          <div class="article-body"><p><strong data-stringify-type="bold">Was Behance content used to train Adobe Firefly?</strong><br>No, Behance content was not used for training the first model of Firefly.<br><br><strong data-stringify-type="bold">Can I post AI-generated art to Behance? </strong><br>Yes, you can share AI-generated art projects to Behance. All projects, including generative art projects, must follow our <a class="c-link" href="https://www.behance.net/misc/community" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer" data-stringify-link="https://www.behance.net/misc/community" data-sk="tooltip_parent">community guidelines</a> and the <a class="c-link" href="https://wwwimages2.adobe.com/content/dam/cc/en/legal/servicetou/Behance-Additional-Terms-en_US-20221001.pdf" target="_blank" rel="noopener" data-stringify-link="https://wwwimages2.adobe.com/content/dam/cc/en/legal/servicetou/Behance-Additional-Terms-en_US-20221001.pdf" data-sk="tooltip_parent">Behance Terms of Use</a>.<br><br><strong data-stringify-type="bold">How do I know a project was made with generative AI models?</strong><br>We encourage all projects, including those made with Generative AI, to be tagged and labeled with the tools used to create them.  You can add and edit tags and tools in your project settings when creating a Behance project. Additionally, we are exploring automated ways to detect and tag work created using generative AI models.  We currently support and will expand the use of Content Credentials throughout Behance to help provide provenance and transparency about the origins of content.</p></div>
          
        </div>
      </section>

  --be-switch-border-active-hover: var(--be-color-blue-700);

  /* Beance tooltips */
  --be-tooltip-bg-primary: var(--be-color-grey-900);
  --be-tooltip-bg-secondary: var(--be-color-white);
  --be-tooltip-text-primary: var(--be-color-white);
  --be-tooltip-text-secondary: var(--be-color-grey-900);

  /* Behance identity colors */
  --be-brand-color: var(--be-color-blue-500);
  --be-accent-color: var(--be-color-blue-500);
  --be-cover-placeholder: var(--be-color-grey-300);

  /* Add placeholders for profile page */
  --be-add-placeholder-border: var(--be-color-grey-700);
  --be-add-placeholder-icon: var(--be-color-white);
  --be-add-placeholder-icon-bg: var(--be-color-grey-700);

  /* Pro button */
  --be-pro-button-start: rgba(1, 136, 253, 1);
  --be-pro-button-middle: rgba(0, 59, 255, 1);
  --be-pro-button-end: rgba(0, 31, 170, 1);

  /* Analytics */
  --be-analytics-placeholder-bg-primary: var(--be-color-grey-700);
  --be-analytics-placeholder-bg-secondary: var(--be-color-grey-700);

  /* TODO --be-profile-info-container-bg can be removed and replaced with --be-bg-secondary when left sidebar refactor is complete */
  --be-profile-info-container-bg: var(--be-bg-primary);

  /* Banners */
  --be-warning-banner-bg: var(--be-bg-secondary);
  --be-warning-banner-circle-border: rgba(var(--be-color-orange-500-rgb), 0.3);
  --be-warning-banner-border-left: var(--be-color-orange-500);
  --be-warning-banner-icon-bg: var(--be-color-orange-500);

  /* Badges */
  /* Green */
  --be-badge-bg-green: rgba(var(--be-color-green-300-rgb), 0.2);
  --be-badge-text-green: var(--be-color-green-300);

  /* Transparent Grey */
  --be-badge-border-transparent-grey: var(--be-color-grey-700);
  --be-badge-text-transparent-grey: var(--be-color-white);

  /* Card */
  --be-card-background-color: var(--be-bg-primary);
  --be-card-border-color: var(--be-border-primary);
  --be-card-border-hover: var(--be-border-primary-hover);
  --be-card-text-color: var(--be-text-primary);
  --be-card-focus-outline-color: var(--be-accessibility-outline-color);
}

What once were simple tool labels have now evolved into rich, textual, and visual descriptors that guide users on how to apply them effectively.

As we continue to improve the user experience in our products, we're excited to bring even more  rich tooltips into our applications. We're looking to commission a talented animator to create short, explanatory, stylized animations for our primary tools in Premiere Pro, including:

-Pen
- Rectangle/Ellipse/Polygon
- Hand
- Zoom 
- Type
- Vertical Type
- Generative Extend
- Stabilize

Each animation will be just a few seconds long, showcasing the most straightforward application of the tool in a fun and relatable way.

These animations should match the style of rich tooltips in our other applications: https://adobe.design/stories/process/designing-adobe-illustrator-s-rich-tooltips 

If you have a passion for illustration, animation, and video tools, we'd love to hear from you!

We love seeing original, human-made creativity shine through in all commissioned work created with Adobe tools. While generative AI can be a helpful part of the creative process, it should only play a supporting role—unless the project brief specifically says otherwise. This project will begin sometime after July 8th. 

Description:
We’re creating a sound effects library designed to bring motion, energy, and personality to video edits. From quick cuts to stylish transitions, audio can transform how a moment feels—and we want your help designing the sounds that do just that. 

This project is focused on Whoosh Sound Effects—those fast, sweeping audio cues that add flair to visual transitions like scene changes, zooms, swipes, fades, and wipes. A great whoosh makes everything feel smoother, snappier, and more intentional. Think of them as the punctuation marks in a video editor’s toolkit—subtle or bold but always helping to guide the viewer’s attention. 

If you're into sound design, playful audio experimentation, or creating effects that feel modern and satisfying, this is your chance to shape what creators will hear when they make their videos pop. 

You could even record yourself making the sounds. If you're into Foley and can make cool sounds, we would love to hear them. 

Budget: $1250 

Project Overview: 
Create a pack of original 15–30 short sound effects (1–3 seconds). Think whooshes, sparkles, glitched tones, comedic pops, or effects no one’s heard before. 

Timeline: 
Final original audio files should be delivered by October.

  --be-input-border-hover: var(--be-color-grey-600);
  --be-input-border-active: var(--be-color-white);
  --be-input-border-error: var(--be-color-red-500);

  --be-dropdown-text-primary: var(--be-color-white);
  --be-dropdown-text-selected: var(--be-color-blue-500);
  --be-dropdown-text-hover: var(--be-color-white);
  --be-dropdown-bg: var(--be-color-grey-900);
  --be-dropdown-bg-hover: var(--be-color-blue-500);
  --be-dropdown-down-arrow: var(--be-color-grey-900);
  --be-dropdown-down-arrow-disabled: var(--be-color-grey-500);

  --be-switch-bg: var(--be-color-grey-600);
  --be-switch-bg-hover: var(--be-color-grey-500);
  --be-switch-bg-active: var(--be-color-blue-500);
  --be-switch-bg-active-hover: var(--be-color-blue-700);
  --be-switch-handle-bg: var(--be-color-white);
  --be-switch-border: var(--be-color-grey-600);
  --be-switch-border-hover: var(--be-color-grey-500);
  --be-switch-border-active: var(--be-color-blue-500);
  --be-switch-border-active-hover: var(--be-color-blue-700);

  /* Beance tooltips */
  --be-tooltip-bg-primary: var(--be-color-grey-900);
  --be-tooltip-bg-secondary: var(--be-color-white);
  --be-tooltip-text-primary: var(--be-color-white);
  --be-tooltip-text-secondary: var(--be-color-grey-900);

  /* Behance identity colors */
  --be-brand-color: var(--be-color-blue-500);
  --be-accent-color: var(--be-color-blue-500);
  --be-cover-placeholder: var(--be-color-grey-300);

  --be-add-placeholder-border: var(--be-color-grey-700);
  --be-add-placeholder-icon: var(--be-color-white);

  --be-pro-button-middle: rgba(0, 59, 255, 1);

  --be-analytics-placeholder-bg-primary: var(--be-color-grey-700);
  --be-analytics-placeholder-bg-secondary: var(--be-color-grey-700);

  --be-warning-banner-bg: var(--be-bg-secondary);
  --be-warning-banner-circle-border: rgba(var(--be-color-orange-500-rgb), 0.3);
  --be-warning-banner-border-left: var(--be-color-orange-500);

  /* Green */

  --be-badge-text-green: var(--be-color-green-300);

  /* Transparent Grey */
  --be-badge-border-transparent-grey: var(--be-color-grey-700);
  --be-badge-text-transparent-grey: var(--be-color-white);

  /* Card */
  --be-card-background-color: var(--be-bg-primary);
  --be-card-border-color: var(--be-border-primary);
  --be-card-border-hover: var(--be-border-primary-hover);
  --be-card-text-color: var(--be-text-primary);
